answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, any switch or lapse in supply carries acute delivery risk. Memory_c1 shows the incumbent has delivered stable, uninterrupted service across cycles, and memory_c4 (verified) indicates that benchmarking against market rates previously moved this or a similar incumbent on both price and terms without disrupting continuity. Memory_c6 corroborates that structuring the incumbent deal (e.g., multi-year volume commitment) can lower unit cost further. Switching primary vendors (memory_c2) or deferring (memory_c5) both introduce timing/onboarding risk incompatible with a 14-day window and zero production buffer, and memory_c2's cost savings history doesn't address the delivery-risk constraint. Renewing outright without renegotiation leaves the 18% cost mandate unaddressed. Negotiating terms with the incumbent before the deadline is the only path that plausibly satisfies both the cost mandate and the no-added-risk constraint, leveraging proven relationship stability. This is the single decision slot for this cycle and applies to the full primary contract, so it is scoped as a full-scale action rather than a limited test, but the actual savings achieved and whether it fully meets the 18% target remain uncertain until the negotiation concludes.
